newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar ends down down on improved supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar ends down down on improved supply.

text.p: Indian sugar ended down on Tuesday on poor consumer demand and improved supply from mills, dealers said.
In ready delivery, sugar S/30 fell five rupees to 1,455/1,480 rupees per quintal, while sugar M/30 dropped to 1,480/1,528 rupees per quintal, they said.
"Higher offerings by millers has pumped more sugar into the market," Shantilal Dedhiya, Secretary to Bombay Sugar Merchants' Association said.
Sugar mill delivery fell five-ten rupees to 1,390 rupees/1,400 rupees per quintal for S/30 variety and to 1,410 rupees/1,425 rupees per quintal for M/30, dealers said.
"Though the free sale quota for the current month is lower, prices were subdued due to lower off-take," Dedhiya said. "But they may bounce back if demand comes in."
Free sale quota for July is 0.75 million tonnes, against 0.80 million last month.
